title: Grateful Dead Live at Electric Factory on 1969-02-14
lineage: SBD > MC > C > C(?) > D > CD > SHN

ai_review.summary: A raw, powerful 1969 Philadelphia show captured on a slightly muffled soundboard tape with hiss, but highlighted by a stellar Dark Star and tight Jerry‑Phil interplay.
ai_review.review: Fans rave about the historic first‑time Philly performance, calling it a hidden gem driven by an intense Dark Star, a searing "The Eleven" and electrifying moments in the Cryptical suite. The recording is a soundboard capture that suffers from constant hiss and a bit of muff‑ness—reminiscent of an old cassette—but all instruments remain audible enough to enjoy the show.

ai_rating.rationale: The musical performance is consistently praised (many 4‑5 star comments) while the audio quality is described as fair/muffled, yielding an overall strong rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Not crystal clear; constant hiss gives it a cassette‑tape vibe and the mix is slightly muffled, but all channels are discernible and instruments can be heard.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A raw, energetic first set that builds into a powerful second half; the band’s interplay—especially Jerry and Phil—is highlighted throughout, making the show feel both historic and tightly woven.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for his tone on Dark Star, the round motif in The Eleven, and soaring leads in the Cryptical suite.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for tight bass interplay with Jerry during The Eleven, adding a Lovelight‑style baseline under the guitar.
